answer: Velvet-Inlet PUF: each agent’s secure enclave probes its MEMS acoustic inlet with velvet noise and a randomized raven-call mask, deriving a device-unique response. For every action, the coordinator sends a nonce; the enclave must return a fresh signed response tied to the inlet’s live microscopic acoustic entropy. The scarce resource is unclonable acoustic entropy, so one device cannot mint many identities. Attacker cost: acquiring and maintaining many distinct inlet-enclave pairs and defeating physical PUF cloning.
